text.p: A stronger escudo and a European Commission report putting Portugal on track for the single currency were lifting bond prices on Wednesday.
Traders said that the greatest support was for bonds up to five years, while the 10-year sector was seen maintaining the spread with the German Bund of 92 basis points.
Few analysts expect the Bank of Portugal to cut rates on Thursday when it announces terms for the next commercial bank reserve period but cuts are certain eventually, they say.
"The spread in the 10 years should remain around 90 basis points today," said one trader. "Below that level, it becomes attractive to take profit," added another.
Traders said that while the shorter end had the greatest potential for gain, volumes were thin due to a lack of sellers.
"The spreads at the short end of the yield curve with Spain are wide, unjustified and are going to have to decline. There is only way for the curve to go...to steepen," said another analyst.
